questions.q: Which feature identifies cerebellar cortex rather than cerebral cortex?
options: Purkinje-cell row between molecular and granular layers
questions.explain: Cerebellar cortex has three layers with Purkinje cells; cerebral cortex has six.

questions.q: Which neuroglial cell forms myelin around axons in the central nervous system?
questions.explain: Oligodendrocytes form CNS myelin. A single oligodendrocyte can extend processes to myelinate segments of several axons.

questions.q: A peripheral nerve is examined in cross-section. Which cell forms the myelin sheath around an individual peripheral axon segment?
questions.explain: Schwann cells myelinate peripheral nervous system axons, with each myelinating Schwann cell forming one internode of a single axon.

questions.q: Which glial cell contributes to the blood–brain barrier by providing end-feet around CNS capillaries?
questions.explain: Astrocytic end-feet surround CNS capillaries and help maintain the blood–brain barrier and the neural microenvironment; endothelial tight junctions form its principal physical seal.

questions.q: Which cells line the ventricles of the brain and the central canal of the spinal cord?
questions.explain: Ependymal cells form the epithelial-like lining of the ventricular system and central canal. Specialised ependymal cells contribute to the choroid plexus.

questions.q: A sensory ganglion contains large neuronal cell bodies surrounded closely by a continuous layer of small supporting cells. What are these supporting cells?
questions.explain: Satellite glial cells surround neuronal cell bodies in peripheral ganglia and regulate their local chemical environment. Schwann cells are associated mainly with axons.
